name: Cliffs of Moher
summary: The western sea-cliffs: Tir Urphost and its covered lamps, the cliff dwellers on the strand below, the koalinth caves, the winds and the fogs, and the light that swings on the top.

facts.text: The Cliffs of Moher (Aillte an Mhothair) are named for a ruined promontory fort, Mothar, that once stood at their southern end, where the headland is called the Hag's Head.
In Irish folklore a fetch is the apparition of a living person, a double whose appearance foretells a death.

Zone 203 (region 200, x 221,184-286,720, y 417,792-483,328): 534 monsters. Tir Urphost (area at 248,267/437,989) is the village: Druid Tobryn, Sentinel Casidhe, Pethos, Maible, merchants and a stable; Brother Esras, Druid Harkin, Aengus Osrithe, Lomond, Doran and Dartan live along the cliffs. The Koalinth Caverns entrance is at 247,379/472,830.

story:
The Cliffs of Moher are the western edge of the realm, a wall of dark stone that falls straight into the sea, and the people who live along them live in two halves. On the top, in the wind, is Tir Urphost, a village of fishers and druids whose boats go down to the water by a path nobody else would use. At the bottom, on the narrow strand where the cliffs meet the sea, are the cliff dwellers, an older people with spears and hunting-packs who say the strand was theirs before any boat came, and who have never once been on good terms with the village above.

The quarrel is old and has a ghost in it. In the days before the koalinth and before the isle rose in the west, the cliffs had a watcher, a man of the cliff-dweller families called Tawi Shon, who kept a fire on the highest point so the boats coming home in the dark would know where the rocks were. He kept it forty winters. Then it went out one storm night and his sons' boat broke under him. The fishers say he fell asleep; the cliff dwellers say the fishers put it out themselves to wreck a Midgard trader, with his sons aboard. Either way he walked off the cliff in the morning, and walks there still with a lamp, and the boats that steer by it break. That is why every lamp on the cliff path of Tir Urphost is covered at night.

The cliff-top belongs to the wind. The gales come in off the sea in a mob, small wild airs that the village children chase and the village elders do not, and behind them the zephyrs and the zephyr wraiths and, on the hill south-east of the crazy lurikeen Doran's camp, a greater zephyr the village calls Sinech, whom the realm's young are sent to clear the lesser winds from. The fogs come in after the wind. Fog wraiths and mist wraiths walk in them, and fog phantoms, and in the fogs on the inland side the fetches stand: doubles of living people, the fishers say, and to meet your own is to know you will not see the year out. A smith from Mag Mell called Ceard was found wandering the beach past the fogs once, robbed and confused, and he has never said what he saw.

The sea brought the koalinth. They came up into the caves under the cliffs in the spring that Hy Brasil left the mist, the fishers of Tir Urphost say, the same spring the fishers saw the isle rise and the sea ran cold, and their caves open on the cliff-top now. Druid Tobryn of the village sends the young down after the stone and the fungus that keep his old seal. The koalinth slinkers walk the strand with the tidal sheeries, and a named tidal sheerie called Aessa keeps a necklace's secret. Further along the sea-shelf the Fanged Sinach hunts the shallows.

Inland the cliffs soften into heath and old grove. The grovewoods of the ancient grove stand there, and the siabra keep a camp among the moheran distorters where they once held a druid of the realm, Harkin, until the young came and freed him. Brother Esras keeps a hermitage on the southern cliffs. Aengus Osrithe and Lomond and Dartan have their own reasons for living out here and keep them.

Why does it matter? Because the Cliffs of Moher are where the realm first saw the west change. The fishers of Tir Urphost were the first Hibernians to see Hy Brasil rise out of the mist, and the first to meet what came up out of the sea after it. Every fisher on the cliffs keeps a covered lamp, a rope, and an opinion about whose fault the fire was, and Tawi Shon still swings his light on the highest point on storm nights.
legend: Cliffs of Moher, the west coast of the old country, levels 15-55. Tir Urphost on the cliff-top is the village (Druid Tobryn's The Broken Seal for the Koalinth Caverns, whose entrance is on the cliffs). The cliff-top is 16-33: Gale (44 of them, Eoghan's Spell), rock and grass sheeries, fetch and bocan, fog and mist wraiths, zephyrs (Sinech, 35, The West Wind). The strand below is 34-44 and social: cliff dwellers, hunters, spearmen (Piaras and Lhia), cliff hangers, koalinth slinkers, tidal sheeries (Aessa for Catch of the Day). Named: Tawi Shon (55 ghost) on the highest point, Coimirceoir (43), Fanged Sinach (43) in the shallows, Brarn (40), the Grey Man (31). Mind the edge: falling off the Cliffs of Moher is its own fight. Village custom: keep your lamp covered on the cliff path at night, and never look a fetch in the face.

loremaster.intro: The Cliffs of Moher, the realm's western wall. [Tir Urphost] keeps the top; the [cliff dwellers] keep the strand. Between them is a [fire] that went out. The [winds] and the [fogs] own the heath, and the [koalinth] came up out of the sea.

topics.Tir Urphost: The fishers' and druids' village on the cliff-top, whose boats go down by a path nobody else would use. Every lamp on its cliff path is covered at night. Druid Tobryn and Sentinel Casidhe live there.
topics.cliff dwellers: The older people of the strand under the cliffs, with spears and hunting-packs, who say the strand was theirs before any boat came. They have never been on good terms with [Tir Urphost].
topics.fire: The boats' fire on the highest point, kept forty winters by Tawi Shon until it went out and his sons' boat broke. The fishers and the [cliff dwellers] blame each other. He walks there still with a lamp.
topics.winds: The gales of the cliff-top, which come in a mob, and the zephyrs behind them. A greater zephyr the village calls Sinech keeps the hill south-east of the crazy lurikeen Doran's camp.
topics.fogs: The fogs that follow the wind: fog wraiths, mist wraiths, fog phantoms, and the fetches, doubles of the living. To meet your own fetch is to know you will not see the year out.
topics.koalinth: The sea-people who came up into the caves under the cliffs the spring Hy Brasil left the mist. Their caves open on the cliff-top. Druid Tobryn sends the young down for his broken seal.
topics.Harkin: A druid of the realm the cliff siabra once held in their camp among the moheran distorters, until the young came for him. He writes to Tir Urphost now.
topics.Esras: Brother Esras, who keeps a hermitage on the southern cliffs and wrote down what the wind told him, which was mostly about the fishers.
topics.Grey Man: Cinead the healer keeps the top of the guard post near Tir Urphost and has not slept well since the Grey Man came. He is a cliff dweller, by his shape, or was, and he haunts the slope south-west of the village, and the fishers who see him come home with the shakes. Cinead sends the young as far as Treibh Caillte, Bri Leith and Mount Collory for what is needed to face him. Lough Gur's grey man is a fog. This one is not.
topics.Chief Whelihan: Chief Whelihan is the chief of the cliff dweller band that camps near the highest point, where Tawi Shon kept his fire, and he is one of the rowdy kind, big and loud and quick to quarrel. The cliff dwellers of the strand do not count him as theirs: his people came up off the strand to live on top, the fire quarrel says, and Whelihan has never forgiven Tir Urphost for covering its lamps.
topics.Bran the Giant: Bran the Giant is a man, the cliff people say, who has grown, and he keeps the heath east of the cliffs with half of a map. The map shows where Nuada's silver wrist lies under the Silvermine, and Bran will send the young about the realm for sap and ale and a reading of it, and then, when they come back to him, he will try to kill them for it, because he wants the other half. Chief Proinnsias of Howth wants to hear where the wrist is. Mikka of Caille has the rest.
topics.Gala: The gales of the cliff-top come in off the sea in a mob, little wild airs that knock over anything left standing, and Gala is the one the village children say leads them, though gales follow nobody. She is the same shape as the rest, and pale as they are, and as big as the biggest, and the Tir Urphost children say that when she blows through the village the doors that were shut come open and the doors that were open bang shut.
topics.Gale: The gales are the small wild airs of the cliff-top, dozens of them, pale and quick and full of whatever they last blew over. They come in off the sea in a mob behind the fog, and the village children chase them and the elders do not. Eoghan of Lough Derg, who works a spell, wants a sprig of vervain, and the gales carry it, because a gale that blew across a druid's garden on its way inland never quite lets go of the garden.

book.title: Notes from a Hermitage on the Cliffs, by Brother Esras
pages: I came out to the southern cliffs to be alone with the wind and discovered that the wind is never alone. It comes in off the sea in a mob, the gales, little wild airs that knock over anything left standing, and the zephyrs come behind them like older brothers, and behind the zephyrs the fog. I have been here eleven winters. I have learned to tell the winds apart. The village children say the greatest of them, on the hill to the south, is a woman named Sinech. I have not met her. I have heard her.

Tir Urphost covers its lamps. Strangers think it is thrift. It is the ghost. The cliffs had a watcher once who kept a fire on the highest point for the boats, and the fire went out, and his sons drowned, and he walked off in the morning. The fishers say he slept at his post. The strand people say the fishers wrecked a trader with his sons aboard. I have asked both, many times, and I believe neither, and I keep my own lamp covered when I walk to the village, because it costs nothing, and he is still up there.

The fog brings the fetches. They stand on the inland heath in the grey and look like people you know, and some of them look like you, and the fishers say that to meet your own is to know you will not see the year out. I met a woman's fetch on the path one morning and told her of it that evening, and she laughed, and she is still alive, so I do not know what the fishers know. I do know that I did not look the fetch in the face. Nobody here does.

The spring the isle came out of the mist in the west, the sea ran cold along these cliffs, and the koalinth came up into the caves below the village. The fishers saw the isle first; the druids of Tir Urphost say we were the first to see what the isle's rising did to the sea. Tobryn keeps an old seal against the caves and sends the young down to mend it. I pray for them, in the wind, which is the only place out here prayers go, and the wind, I have found, takes them somewhere.
